exposure: Breastfeeding practices (delayed initiation time, less frequency of breastfeeding, duration of breastfeeding sessions)
cohort: The study included full-term newborns admitted with serum sodium concentrations of >=145 mEq/L (cases) and healthy control mother-baby pairs at a tertiary care rural hospital.
finding: Delayed initiation of breastfeeding, inadequate breastfeeding techniques, maternal breast-related issues, and primiparous mothers were significant contributors to neonatal hypernatremic dehydration (NHD) in full-term, exclusively breastfed neonates, with an observed incidence of 4.7%.
cross-section timing: The average neonatal age at presentation with NHD was six days.
